utterances.text: After I was invited, a vehicle arrived from Belgrade, belonging to our unit, I was transported to our headquarters in Belgrade, and we received instructions there. They told us that if we had any documents, they should be left behind for our own personal safety, our driving licence and everything else that could disclose our identity, that was to be left in the office of the headquarters. After that, as we arrived at different times, as soon as a group had been formed, they told us to go and have a walk around town so as to avoid having a crowd of people in front of the building itself. I don't know how much time within the by, but we gathered together again, and a sort of lecture -- we were given a lecture about morale and so on. And we were told that we would be going to the theatre of war, to Bosnia. We weren't told which part of Bosnia or the objectives of the operation. But after that, the buses arrived. We were taken by bus to --

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Can I interrupt you for one moment? Who was it who was giving you this talk, and were the people that you were joining up with any of them people you had known from the Super Tigers?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-020
utterances.text: All the Super Tigers responded. I can't say we all did, but we did in large numbers. Then there were members of other units from the support and reinforcement units, and this morale boosting talk was held by Legija and Arkan himself.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Thank you. And back to the buses, and use the map as you need to.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-020
utterances.text: After that, we were taken to a place called Lipovacka Suma, which is close by Belgrade, which is where the barracks were belonging to the special police, and they were waiting for us there because people from other buses were turning up, not only our people, but buses with others too. We stayed there for a very brief period of time. I can't tell you how long exactly. But after that we were sent to Petrova Gora. No. It was to Mount Tara, Mount Tara, where we stayed for several days so that we could organise ourselves to go to the theatre of war. And to prevent us from getting bored, although we were wearing civilians clothes as we arrived, we would have a theoretical brush-up course on mines, infantry training and so on and so forth, and we would move around the territory, but we were in civilian clothes, so we couldn't move around too much. It would have been silly to move around the forest area and so on. Then we returned from Mount Tara, back to Lipovacka Suma, where we went to the barracks and were given -- we were issued weapons very quickly. They just handed out the rifles and smaller weapons. There was no record of this, not to use it, but to put it in the buses so they could be transported further afield. And a column was organised there, except for the buses, there were trailers there too with the different military Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. equipment and materiel, trailer trucks. And we started out towards Bosnia, the border with Bosnia. Where we crossed the border, actually, I can't say, but I do know that the border crossing was somewhere nearby Bijeljina. Whether it was Zeljeznicki Most, the railway bridge or Pavlovica Cuprija I don't know, but we had to wait --

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Pause there. Looking at the map and using the pointer, can you just indicate in general where the Tara place was where you went first?

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: The Court can also find it on the atlas at page 33, in the north-west corner.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-020
utterances.text: I can't see anything on this small map.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Well, can you just give us the rough -- if you can't, it doesn't matter, but if you can give us the rough area of the Tara mountain on the map, we'd be grateful.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Meanwhile, while that's happening, Your Honour --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-020
utterances.text: Found it.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Your Honours see he pointed -- that's the shape that he points there is reflected in the top right-hand corner of page 33 of the atlas, which of course shows the western boundary of Serbia and the eastern boundary of Bosnia.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: So that's where you went first. And staying with this map, can you just -- I'm sure the Judges know, but for others viewing, can you just give a rough indication of where it was you crossed into Bosnia?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-020
utterances.text: We crossed Bosnia -- into Bosnia around the Bijeljina area.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: I imagine the Judges will all know where that is. And then where did you go after that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-020
utterances.text: After Bijeljina, we set off through the corridor towards Bosnia. We didn't know the exact location until we actually arrived there. We didn't know the direction we were going in. But the next day we ended up the Petrova Gora itself.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Very well. Can you point that out on the map for us?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-020
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: And just, having found it -- there we are. Thank you. So you went through the corridor on the north of Bosnia, passing into Bosnia somewhere in the region of Bijeljina, that is, on the north-east of Bosnia, and then emerged into Petrova Gora in Croatia?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-020
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Petrova Gora can be found in the atlas at page 20, in square B3. It's quite well marked, just to the north or north-west of Velika Kladusa. While in Petrova Gora, what happened?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-020
utterances.text: At Petra Gora we stopped off for about one, two, or three days. I can't say exactly now. We were waiting for everything to be organised and to receive orders as to where we were to head for. We were given equipment, and the rifles were issued, not like they were beforehand, when we were just handed them out for transport purposes. We were issued weapons and we were divided up into combat units, so that each combat unit was issued the equipment and weapons they needed. And then we were send off to the area and a place called Katinovac.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Before we come to that, the place where you were -- and where you were given your equipment, did you discover that it was a headquarters of some kind?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-020
utterances.text: It was a logistics base. I would call it that, because there were stockpiles of fuel and weapons, and a landing strip, takeoff strip for helicopters, and a hospital, and the staff was there, too the headquarters.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: The man Frenki, did he feature as having any significance at this base or not?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-020
utterances.text: That was not -- he was not directly our commander, but he was the commander to our commander, so he was a leading personage there. I don't know whether to call him the main commander or something else.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Included in the equipment you were provided and clothing you were provided, were there berets; if so, of what colour and with what badge or other insignia?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-020
utterances.text: Of course we were issued berets so that we could be like the other units stationed there, and there was a sword with the three Cs in Cyrillic, with our flag. That was the insignia.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Four Cs, Sorry. Interpreter's mistake. Ss.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: And the colour of the berets?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-020
utterances.text: Red.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: One last detail. You effectively covered it, but I'd like you to be clear, paragraph 56. When you were first driven from Belgrade to Lipovacka Suma, who was driving the buses and how were they dressed?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-020
utterances.text: Some of the drivers were policemen, and the buses, some of them belonged to the police and the rest had civilian number plates. They were Belgrade buses.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Equipped in the way you had been in Petrova Gora and you say that the rifles were issued, does that mean they were issued with unique numbers against individual soldiers? Is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-020
utterances.text: Yes. There were serial numbers, but I can't say whether each soldier -- the names weren't stated. It was just so-and-so, one weapon or 20, 30, or however many were issued, for one platoon.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Then your first order, once you were properly equipped, was given by who, and it was to do what? Paragraph 62, page 25.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-020
utterances.text: The first order -- or rather, the order we received was in the form of instructions, that it was our job to train the army of National Defence from Western Bosnia. Because at that time there was a clash in Bosnia between Fikret Abdic and the 5th Corps. The army of Fikret Abdic was the Army of Defence of Western Bosnia, and we were supposed to train them in combat action, which would follow in the next couple of days. It wasn't any major training. It was just three or four days of training to explain to the men how they should move in formation, et cetera.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: And Velika Kladusa, which I've already drawn to the Judges' attention on page 20 of the atlas, was that the place to which you went, or to that area?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-020
utterances.text: The area around Velika Kladusa, because Velika Kladusa was still under the corps's control.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: And at this stage of events, by whom was Fikret Abdic's army being equipped in part?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-020
utterances.text: The weapons themselves and the clothing, they probably had to fend for themselves. The weapons, however, had mostly come from us, because they had already been expelled out of that territory. They did have some weapons, but some older trophy weapons, automatics from World War II, things like that. That belonged to them, or they had got it from somewhere. I can't really say. But the better type of equipment, automatic rifles, et cetera, they got from us.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Did you participate in battles for some time there?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-020
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Indeed, until the liberation, as described, of Velika Kladusa, and also in the same square of the map.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Perhaps we can just place this on the overhead projector at page 20, bottom right-hand part of the page, Vrnograc.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-020
utterances.text: I didn't participate until the liberation of Velika Kladusa, because prior to the liberation of Velika Kladusa I was wounded.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: We can see on the map Velika Kladusa and, east of that, Vrnograc. And were the units you described deployed, at any event, in battles in these areas?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-020
utterances.text: Which units do you have in mind?

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: We're speaking of yourself, your own unit.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-020
utterances.text: Yes, our units did participate, my unit specifically, and other units who came with us, who also wore red berets.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Did there come a time, however, when the Red Berets - paragraph 64 - had sustained some losses?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-020
utterances.text: Our group did. Within three or four days, we had three casualties, and more than half of us were wounded.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: And were there actual losses, and were those losses associated with a stopping of direct involvement of the Red Berets in these operations?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-020
utterances.text: Initially, as far as I know, we did not fully uphold the orders we were given, because we were not supposed to participate directly in operations, only in coordination of actions. However, initially we did participate in operations themselves. We suffered losses. And then later on, we were split into groups that were in charge of training, observation, and further coordination of new operations.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Was there a lieutenant with the first name Jugoslav, known as Jugo? What happened to him in your unit? What happened to him?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-020
utterances.text: During the Rajnovac operation he was killed by the mosque.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Was there another DB officer, whose name you're unable to recall, who fell on the field?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-020
utterances.text: I can't tell you exactly whether he was an officer of the DB. He was a commander of the special police unit, which at the time was stationed in our barracks in Erdut. And then after the withdrawal of the Serb volunteer guards, special police were sent into those barracks, and he led it, and I think his nickname was Kole. I believe he was a colonel. After he died, his picture was printed among the death notices in Belgrade daily Vecernje Novosti, and it was said that he died defending his homeland.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Can we go briefly, or fairly briefly, into private session for the next page and a half, and then back into public session at the end.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We're back into open session, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: C-020, with units deployed in the area under Frenki's command, were there instructions as to how you were or were not allowed to have yourselves identified? What, if anything, were you to do about your having come from Serbia?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-020
utterances.text: We received instructions from Legija prior to setting out. We were told that we were not allowed to say what unit we actually belonged to. Instead of our insignia, we did not use any insignia, and we were not allowed to reveal that we were members of our actual unit. We were told that if we came into a situation where we had to say, and only in front of our personnel, our people, we were to say that we were members of special police from Serbia. And if we fell into enemies' hands, then we were not allowed to say anything.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: As to your red berets, did you wear those on combat operations or not?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-020
utterances.text: As far as the first two operations are concerned, after them we saw that the terrain wasn't in accordance with that. And after that, we had woolen hats and camouflage hats. That's what we wore afterwards.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Were you allowed to reveal yourself as, in any way, Arkan's men?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-020
utterances.text: It wasn't directly banned, but we were told it wasn't a good idea because there was Muslim population there, and even though this was Western Bosnia, they still didn't have a good opinion about Arkan's men.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: How were you paid, and where?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-020
utterances.text: We received part of the money right there, in the field; and then the other part was sent to the headquarters. And when we went home, since after a certain number of battles we would go home for a brief while in groups, then the second part of the money we would receive in headquarters itself.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Fikret Abdic's part of Bosnia was divided into how many operational zones?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-020
utterances.text: As far as I know, into two tactical groups.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: One commanded by --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-020
utterances.text: One Tactical Group was under the command of us, that is, Legija, and the other one -- our group was called Tactical Group 2, and the commander of Tactical Group 1 was Rajo Bozovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Your Honour, there's a video which is going to be produced by the next witness, and I think it's four minutes long. I have extracted from it, or there have been extracted from it two stills. I think the purpose to which we would put that video to this witness is better served by showing him the two stills, and you can then associate the stills with the video when it's played with the next witness. How we deal with that in terms of exhibit formalities, I'm not sure, but it will save time and I think will be more efficient. Please put them on the ELMO. Apparently the video is cued for -- it's a one-minute clip so we might play it as well, but--

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Can you tell us, please, who in this picture you can identify?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-020
utterances.text: This is a picture from the parade at Slunj, and I can identify on the left -- shall I show you?

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Yes, please.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-020
utterances.text: That is Rajo Bozovic, and on the right is Legija. And with his back turned here -- you can't see, but I know this picture from Slunj, that is President Martic.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Perhaps as the video has been cued and it's only a minute, perhaps we can play it. I'd ask the booth to do that, in which case may the video, this part of it, be marked for identification only and then it can be properly produced in due course. So this is the parade in Slunj. Held on what day, please, C-020?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-020
utterances.text: This was called the Vidovdan parade. It was held on the 28th of June, on St. Vitus Day.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Thank you very much. I think, Your Honour, the speed at which identification by video is to be done is asking the impossible sometimes. It may be preferable if we mark the video for identification. And if I arrange to have further copies of those two other photographs produced and, with your leave, make them the seventh tab of this exhibit, and they can be provided later.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Yes. We'll do that.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Then there's just paragraph 71 and 72 to deal with.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: The stills will be marked under Exhibit P347, tab 7.1 and .2.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Did you have one occasion to go and introduce yourself to Frenki, paragraph 72, or to try to introduce yourself to Frenki?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-020
utterances.text: Only once.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Where was that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-020
utterances.text: I was given an order by Legija during the night to go to Petrova Gora to collect some maps that we needed for the next day for our operation, and at the headquarters where I picked up the maps, the order was that I address myself to Frenki. I had never seen that man in my life, and so Legija told me that once I entered, I was to introduce myself and to ask for Frenki.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Did you do that, and did the man Frenki appear?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-020
utterances.text: Yes. He was sitting in the room where the maps were when I introduced myself. The maps were already waiting for me, packed, so it was only a couple of minutes that I was there. And so he just asked me, "So you're the one?" And he mentioned my name.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: And Frenki's height, approximately, and appearance?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-020
utterances.text: In those couple of minutes that one can measure a man, he was about 1 metre, 80; therefore, a tall man, of athletic build. He wore glasses, ordinary glasses; thin hair, brown in colour. I can't be more detailed in my description.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: And what did you know or come to know of the frequency of meetings between Milorad Ulemek and Frenki?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-020
utterances.text: I know that Legija, after every operation, went for coordination purposes, and prior to any operation for coordination purposes, to Petrova Gora. So the story was that he was going to a meeting with Frenki. Now, whether he actually met with Frenki himself or someone from his staff, I can't say.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: That concludes the examination-in-chief. And as I think I forecast, the evidence did not last as long as the size of the summary might have led us to believe.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Cross-examination in the morning. I'm reminded we're sitting tomorrow between 9.00 and 1.00. Witness C-020, could you be back, please, 9.00 tomorrow morning to conclude your evidence. We'll rise now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: be reconvened on Wednesday, the 23rd day of October 2002, at 9.00 a.m.
